sentence: それ、ほんまに言ってるの？
translation: Are you really saying that?
note: Kansai for 本当 (really). ほんまに = 本当に.
wm: really, truly
Kansai for 本当. Hikaru says it constantly: ほんまに, ほんま?
wb: ほんま：Kansai form of 本当 (ほんとう)
sm: They can't believe what the other person just said.
A surprised reaction to a friend.
sb: それ、：that
ほんまに：really (Kansai)
言ってるの？：are you saying? (casual question)
Whole: are you really saying that?
se: Are you really saying that?
Are you seriously saying that?
You really mean that?

sentence: これ、めっちゃいいやん。
translation: This is really good!
note: Kansai-born slang, now used all over Japan.
wm: very, super, really
Casual and very common, especially in Kansai. Stronger and looser than とても.
wb: めっちゃ：casual form of めちゃくちゃ (extremely)
sm: They think this thing is great.
A happy reaction to something they're shown.
sb: これ、：this
めっちゃいいやん。：is really good (やん = isn't it, Kansai)
Whole: this is really good!
se: This is really good!
This is super good!
Oh, this is so good!

sentence: 今日の動画、もう見た？
translation: Did you already watch today's video?
wm: a video, especially an online one
What YouTubers call their uploads. More common than ビデオ for YouTube.
sm: They're asking if the other person has seen the new video yet.
sb: 今日の動画、：today's video
もう見た？：did you already watch? (もう = already)
Whole: did you already watch today's video?
se: Did you already watch today's video?
Have you seen today's video yet?
Did you watch today's upload?

sentence: あいつら、離婚したらしいよ。
translation: I heard those two got divorced.
note: らしい = I heard, apparently.
wm: divorce
離婚する = to get divorced. The opposite of 結婚.
sm: Passing on gossip about a couple.
sb: あいつら、：those guys (casual)
離婚したらしいよ。：apparently divorced
Whole: I hear those two got divorced.
se: I heard those two got divorced.
Apparently they got divorced.
I heard those two split up.

sentence: いろんな人に話を聞いてみた。
translation: I tried asking all kinds of people.
wm: all kinds of, various
The everyday spoken form of 色々な. Always goes before a noun.
wb: いろんな：spoken form of 色々な (いろいろな)
sm: They asked lots of different people about it.
Explaining how they did their research.
sb: いろんな人に：to all kinds of people
話を聞いてみた。：tried listening to what they had to say (てみる = try)
Whole: I tried asking all kinds of people.
se: I tried asking all kinds of people.
I asked a bunch of different people.
I went and asked all sorts of people.

sentence: 結論は、まだ出てない。
translation: There's no conclusion yet.
note: 出てない = 出ていない.
wm: a conclusion, a final answer
Used when a decision or answer is reached. 結論が出る = a conclusion is reached.
wb: Whole: where the discussion ends up.
sm: Talking about a decision still being made.
sb: 結論は、：the conclusion
まだ出てない。：hasn't come out yet
Whole: there's no conclusion yet.
se: There's no conclusion yet.
We haven't reached a conclusion yet.
Nothing's been decided yet.

sentence: 結論から言うと、俺は行かない。
meaning: to cut to the chase, the bottom line is
translation: To cut to the chase, I'm not going.
note: Hikaru opens the video with まず結論から言いますと (the polite form).
wm: to start with the conclusion, the bottom line is
Said before giving the answer first, then the explanation. Polite: 結論から言いますと.
wb: Whole: saying it from the conclusion.
sm: They give their answer first: they won't go.
sb: 結論から言うと、：to cut to the chase
俺は行かない。：I'm not going
Whole: bottom line, I'm not going.
se: To cut to the chase, I'm not going.
Bottom line: I'm not going.
Long story short, I won't go.

sentence: これ、やばくない？
translation: Isn't this insane?
note: やばくない？ = isn't it crazy?
wm: crazy, insane, terrible, amazing
Very casual. Can be bad (dangerous, awful) or good (amazing). Tone tells you which.
wb: やばい：slang adjective, crazy or dangerous
sb: これ、：this
やばくない？：isn't it crazy?
Whole: isn't this insane?
se: Isn't this insane?
This is crazy, right?
Isn't this nuts?

sentence: え、マジで？
translation: Huh, seriously?
note: マジで = seriously.
wm: serious, for real
Casual slang. マジで? = seriously? マジ is also used like very: マジやばい.
wb: マジ：slang from 真面目 (まじめ, serious)
sm: They're surprised by what they just heard.
sb: え、：huh
マジで？：seriously?
Whole: huh, seriously?
se: Huh, seriously?
What, for real?
Wait, seriously?

sentence: あいつ、毎回遅れて来るよな。
translation: That guy comes late every time.
wm: every time
Used for something that happens again and again. Often a little annoyed.
sm: Their friend is late every time.
sb: あいつ、：that guy
毎回：every time
遅れて来るよな。：comes late, right?
Whole: that guy comes late every time.
se: That guy comes late every time.
He's late every single time.
That guy always shows up late.

sentence: 今日はめちゃくちゃ疲れた。
translation: I was super tired today.
wm: extremely, really (also: a total mess)
Casual. めちゃくちゃ疲れた = super tired. On its own, めちゃくちゃ can mean a mess.
wb: めちゃくちゃ：casual word for extremely, or a mess
sb: 今日は：today
めちゃくちゃ疲れた。：was extremely tired
Whole: I was super tired today.
se: I was super tired today.
Today wore me out.
I'm completely exhausted today.

sentence: もう着いてるはずなんだけど。
translation: He should already be there, but...
note: はずなんだけど = should be, but (I'm not sure).
wm: should, is supposed to, is expected to
Says what you expect to be true. はずなのに = even though it should be.
wb: はず：noun for expectation, written 筈
sm: They expected their friend to have arrived by now.
sb: もう：already
着いてるはずなんだけど。：should have arrived, but
Whole: he should already be there, but...
se: He should already be there, but...
He's supposed to be here already...
They should've arrived by now.

sentence: お金に関しては、俺が全部払う。
meaning: as for, when it comes to
translation: When it comes to money, I'll pay for everything.
note: Hikaru: これに関しては (as for this).
wm: as for, regarding, when it comes to
Picks a topic to say something about it. Sounds a bit more serious than は.
wb: 関して：concerning (て-form of 関する)
sm: They'll cover all the money side.
sb: お金に関しては、：when it comes to money
俺が：I
全部払う。：will pay for everything
Whole: as for money, I'll pay it all.
se: When it comes to money, I'll pay for everything.
As for money, I'll cover it all.
Don't worry about money, I'll pay.

sentence: 親に対して、そんな言い方するなよ。
translation: Don't talk like that to your parents.
wm: towards, to, against
Shows who an action or feeling is aimed at. 親に対して = towards your parents.
wb: 対して：facing (て-form of 対する)
sm: They're telling someone off for being rude to their parents.
sb: 親に対して、：towards your parents
そんな言い方：that way of talking
するなよ。：don't do
Whole: don't talk like that to your parents.
se: Don't talk like that to your parents.
Don't speak to your parents like that.
You can't talk to your parents that way.

sentence: 最近、まともにご飯食べてない。
translation: Lately I haven't been eating proper meals.
note: まともに = properly.
wm: proper, decent, normal
まともに = properly. まともな人 = a normal, sensible person.
wb: まとも：word for proper or decent
sm: They've been too busy to eat real meals.
sb: 最近、：lately
まともに：properly
ご飯食べてない。：haven't been eating meals
Whole: lately I haven't eaten properly.
se: Lately I haven't been eating proper meals.
I haven't had a real meal lately.
I've not been eating properly recently.

sentence: この映画、友達に勧められて見た。
translation: A friend recommended this movie, so I watched it.
note: 勧められて = was recommended (passive). お勧め = a recommendation.
wm: to recommend, to suggest
お勧め = recommendation. お勧めしない = I don't recommend it (Hikaru, about 0-day marriage).
sm: They watched a movie because a friend suggested it.
sb: この映画、：this movie
友達に：by a friend
勧められて見た。：was recommended and watched
Whole: a friend recommended this movie, so I watched it.
se: A friend recommended this movie, so I watched it.
I watched this movie on a friend's recommendation.
My friend told me to watch this one.

sentence: 動画のコメント、全部読んでるよ。
translation: I read all the comments on my videos.
wm: a comment
On YouTube and social media. コメントする = to comment.
sm: A YouTuber says they read every comment.
sb: 動画のコメント、：the videos' comments
全部読んでるよ。：I read all of them
Whole: I read all the comments on my videos.
se: I read all the comments on my videos.
I read every comment on my videos.
I go through all the comments.

sentence: コメント欄、全部読んだよ。
translation: I read the whole comment section.
wm: the comment section
Where viewers write under a video. 欄 = a box or section on a page.
sm: They went through all the comments.
sb: コメント欄、：the comment section
全部読んだよ。：read all of it
Whole: I read the whole comment section.
se: I read the whole comment section.
I read everything in the comments.
I went through the whole comment section.

sentence: いつものメンバーで飲みに行こう。
translation: Let's go drinking with the usual crew.
note: 飲みに行こう = let's go drinking.
wm: a member, the people in a group
いつものメンバー = the usual crew, the regular group.
sm: They want to go out with their regular friends.
sb: いつものメンバーで：with the usual crew
飲みに行こう。：let's go drinking
Whole: let's go drinking with the usual crew.
se: Let's go drinking with the usual crew.
Let's go for drinks with the usual gang.
Let's grab a drink with the regular crew.

sentence: 毎日これやるの、しんどいわ。
translation: Doing this every day is exhausting.
note: わ at the end softens it.
wm: tiring, tough, hard to bear
Originally Kansai, now common everywhere. Physical or emotional. Hikaru: 味方されればされるほどしんどい.
wb: しんどい：adjective for exhausting or tough
sm: Doing the same thing every day is wearing them out.
sb: 毎日：every day
これやるの、：doing this
しんどいわ。：is exhausting
Whole: doing this every day is exhausting.
se: Doing this every day is exhausting.
Doing this daily is draining.
It's tough doing this every day.

sentence: 彼女にずっと振り回されてる。
meaning: to jerk around, to drag around
translation: My girlfriend keeps jerking me around.
note: 振り回されてる = being jerked around (passive).
wm: to swing around; to jerk someone around
With people: to make them follow your changing moods. Hikaru: 俺に振り回されて.
sm: Their girlfriend keeps changing her mind and they have to go along with it.
sb: 彼女に：by my girlfriend
ずっと：all the time
振り回されてる。：am being jerked around
Whole: my girlfriend keeps jerking me around.
se: My girlfriend keeps jerking me around.
I'm always being dragged around by my girlfriend.
She keeps messing me around.

sentence: みんなでくじを引こう。
translation: Let's all draw lots.
note: くじを引く = to draw a lot.
wm: a lottery ticket, a lucky draw, lots
くじを引く = to draw one. Hikaru: 大外れくじ = a total dud of a ticket.
wb: くじ：word for a lottery or lot (籤)
sm: They want to decide something by drawing lots.
sb: みんなで：all together
くじを引こう。：let's draw lots
Whole: let's all draw lots.
se: Let's all draw lots.
Let's draw lots together.
Let's all pick a ticket.

sentence: やった、当たりだ！
translation: Yes, a winner!
wm: a win, a hit, a winning ticket
From 当たる (to hit). Also means a good pick: この店は当たり = this shop was a good find.
sm: A reaction to a lottery or draw.
sb: やった、：yes!
当たりだ！：it's a winner
Whole: yes, a winner!
se: Yes, a winner!
Yes, I won!
Yes! It's a hit!

sentence: この店は大外れだったな。
meaning: a total miss, a complete dud
translation: This place was a total miss.
wm: a total miss, a big disappointment
The opposite of 大当たり. Hikaru calls himself 大外れくじ, a total dud ticket.
sb: この店は：this shop
大外れだったな。：was a total miss
Whole: this place was a total miss.
se: This place was a total miss.
This shop was a complete dud.
That place was a huge letdown.

sentence: 夏祭りに行ってきた。
translation: I went to a summer festival.
note: 夏祭り = summer festival.
wm: a festival
Japanese summer festivals have food stalls and lottery games (祭りくじ).
sm: They went to a summer festival.
sb: 夏祭りに：to a summer festival
行ってきた。：went (and came back)
Whole: I went to a summer festival.
se: I went to a summer festival.
I went to a summer festival.
I've been to the summer fair.

sentence: 俺、ちょっとわがままやな。
translation: I'm a bit selfish, huh.
note: やな = だな (Kansai).
wm: selfish, self-centred, spoilt
Doing what you want without thinking of others. Hikaru: 僕がわがまますぎる.
wb: わがまま：word for selfish (我が儘)
sb: 俺、：I
ちょっと：a bit
わがままやな。：am selfish, huh
Whole: I'm a bit selfish, huh.
se: I'm a bit selfish, huh.
I guess I'm kind of selfish.
I'm a little selfish, aren't I.

sentence: 両方ほしいんだけど。
translation: I want both, though.
wm: both
Both of two things or sides. Hikaru: 両方にいい顔をする = to be nice to both sides.
sm: They can't choose between two things.
sb: 両方：both
ほしいんだけど。：want, though
Whole: I want both, though.
se: I want both, though.
I want both of them.
Can I have both?

sentence: 人を傷つけるようなことは言うな。
translation: Don't say things that hurt people.
wm: to hurt, to wound
Often feelings. 傷つく = to get hurt.
wb: Whole: to put a wound on.
sm: They're telling someone to be careful with their words.
sb: 人を：people
傷つけるような：that would hurt
ことは：things
言うな。：don't say
Whole: don't say things that hurt people.
se: Don't say things that hurt people.
Don't say hurtful things.
Don't say anything that'll hurt people.

sentence: これがリアルな生活です。
translation: This is my real life.
wm: real, realistic
Used a lot on YouTube: リアルな生活 = real life, as it really is.
sm: A YouTuber is showing their everyday life as it is.
sb: これが：this is
リアルな生活です。：real life
Whole: this is my real life.
se: This is my real life.
This is what my life is really like.
Here's my real daily life.

sentence: 味はまあまあかな。
translation: The taste is so-so, I guess.
wm: so-so, okay, not bad
Somewhere between good and bad. Also まあまあ (said twice) to calm someone down.
sb: 味は：the taste
まあまあかな。：is so-so, I guess
Whole: the taste is so-so, I guess.
se: The taste is so-so, I guess.
It tastes okay, I suppose.
The flavour's not bad.

sentence: おかしな話だよね。
translation: It's a strange story, isn't it.
wm: strange, odd, funny
Always before a noun. おかしな話 = an odd thing to say, which Hikaru uses.
wb: おかしな：before-noun form of おかしい
sm: They think the situation doesn't make sense.
sb: おかしな話：a strange story
だよね。：isn't it
Whole: it's a strange story, isn't it.
se: It's a strange story, isn't it.
That's a weird thing, right?
It's an odd situation, huh.

sentence: 結婚指輪、どこに置いたっけ？
translation: Where did I put my wedding ring?
note: っけ = I wonder (trying to remember).
wm: a ring (worn on a finger)
結婚指輪 = wedding ring. Hikaru takes his off at the end of the video.
sm: They can't find their wedding ring.
sb: 結婚指輪、：wedding ring
どこに：where
置いたっけ？：did I put it?
Whole: where did I put my wedding ring?
se: Where did I put my wedding ring?
Where'd I leave my wedding ring?
Where did my wedding ring go?

sentence: 会うこと自体、久しぶりやな。
translation: Even just meeting up is a first in ages.
wm: itself, in itself
Picks out the thing itself. 会うこと自体 = meeting up itself.
sm: They haven't even met up in a long time.
Two people meeting after a long break.
sb: 会うこと自体、：meeting up itself
久しぶりやな。：it's been a while (Kansai やな)
Whole: even meeting up has been a long time.
se: Even just meeting up is a first in ages.
Just meeting up is rare now.
Even seeing each other is a first in ages.

sentence: 異性の友達って、いる？
translation: Do you have friends of the opposite sex?
wm: the opposite sex
異性の友達 = a friend of the opposite sex.
sm: They're asking about friends who aren't the same gender.
sb: 異性の友達って、：friends of the opposite sex
いる？：do you have?
Whole: do you have friends of the opposite sex?
se: Do you have friends of the opposite sex?
Any friends of the opposite sex?
Do you have friends who are girls (or guys)?

sentence: 今日は気合い入ってるね。
translation: You're really fired up today.
note: 気合い入ってる = fired up.
wm: fighting spirit, determination
気合いが入る = to be fired up, to make an effort (also with clothes or looks).
sm: Someone has clearly made a big effort today.
sb: 今日は：today
気合い入ってるね。：you're fired up
Whole: you're really fired up today.
se: You're really fired up today.
You've really made an effort today.
You're so pumped today.

sentence: うちら、もう友達やん。
translation: We're friends now, right?
note: やん = じゃない (Kansai).
wm: we, us
Casual, used a lot by women and in Kansai. Hikaru's ex-wife says うちら.
sb: うちら、：we
もう：already
友達やん。：are friends, right (Kansai)
Whole: we're friends now, right?
se: We're friends now, right?
We're already friends.
We're friends now, aren't we?

sentence: スピード結婚だったね。
translation: That was a whirlwind marriage, huh.
note: スピード結婚 = a whirlwind marriage.
wm: speed
スピード結婚 / スピード離婚 = getting married or divorced very fast.
sm: The couple got married very fast.
sb: スピード結婚：whirlwind marriage
だったね。：it was, huh
Whole: that was a whirlwind marriage, huh.
se: That was a whirlwind marriage, huh.
They married really fast, huh.
That was a speed marriage.

sentence: 新しい店がオープンした。
translation: A new shop opened.
wm: open; opening (of a shop)
オープンする = to open. Also open as in honest: オープンな人.
sm: A new shop has just opened.
sb: 新しい店が：a new shop
オープンした。：opened
Whole: a new shop opened.
se: A new shop opened.
A new store just opened.
There's a new shop now.

sentence: この店、もうすぐクローズするらしい。
translation: Apparently this shop is closing soon.
wm: close, closing
クローズする = to close. Hikaru jokes: クローズマリッジ (a closed marriage).
sm: They heard the shop will close soon.
sb: この店、：this shop
もうすぐ：soon
クローズするらしい。：is apparently closing
Whole: apparently this shop is closing soon.
se: Apparently this shop is closing soon.
I heard this place is closing soon.
This shop is shutting down soon.

sentence: 今日もお疲れ様でした。
translation: Thanks for your hard work today too.
wm: thanks for your work, good job
Said at the end of work or a video. お疲れ様でした (polite), お疲れ (casual).
wb: Whole: (you must be) tired, thank you.
sm: They thank everyone at the end of the day.
sb: 今日も：today too
お疲れ様でした。：thanks for your hard work
Whole: thanks for your hard work today too.
se: Thanks for your hard work today too.
Good work today too.
Thanks for today, everyone.

sentence: 机をひっくり返した。
translation: I flipped the desk over.
wm: to flip over, to turn upside down
Also: to overturn a decision or situation.
sm: Someone got angry and flipped their desk.
sb: 机を：the desk
ひっくり返した。：flipped over
Whole: I flipped the desk over.
se: I flipped the desk over.
I turned the desk upside down.
I flipped my desk.

target: ちゃぶ台をひっくり返す
sentence: 最後にちゃぶ台をひっくり返すなよ。
reading: ちゃぶだいをひっくりかえす
meaning: to wreck everything at the last minute
translation: Don't go wrecking everything at the end.
note: Hikaru says he kept doing this throughout the marriage.
wm: to overturn everything, to ruin a plan at the last second
From an old image of an angry father flipping the low dining table (ちゃぶ台).
wb: ひっくり返す：to flip over
Whole: to flip the dining table.
sm: They're asking someone not to ruin everything at the last moment.
Warning a friend before a decision.
sb: 最後に：at the end
ちゃぶ台をひっくり返すなよ。：don't flip the table
Whole: don't go wrecking everything at the end.
se: Don't go wrecking everything at the end.
Don't ruin it all at the last minute.
Don't go flipping the table at the end.

sentence: 弁解はしません。
translation: I won't make excuses.
wm: an excuse, a justification
Formal-ish. 弁解しない = to make no excuses. Hikaru: 弁解の余地はない.
sb: 弁解は：excuses
しません。：I won't make
Whole: I won't make excuses.
se: I won't make excuses.
I'm not going to make excuses.
No excuses from me.

sentence: あいつの考えは全然ぶれない。
translation: That guy's thinking never wavers at all.
wm: to waver, to shake, to be inconsistent
With people: to keep changing your mind. ぶれない = steady, consistent.
wb: ぶれる：verb for shake or waver
sm: Their friend always sticks to his ideas.
sb: あいつの考えは：his way of thinking
全然ぶれない。：doesn't waver at all
Whole: that guy's thinking never wavers.
se: That guy's thinking never wavers at all.
He never changes his mind.
His views are rock solid.

sentence: 前の店とは全然別物やな。
translation: It's totally different from the old shop.
wm: a completely different thing
Used when two things that look similar really aren't. 全然別物 = totally different.
sm: The new shop isn't like the old one at all.
sb: 前の店とは：from the old shop
全然別物やな。：is totally different (Kansai やな)
Whole: it's totally different from the old shop.
se: It's totally different from the old shop.
It's nothing like the old place.
It's a whole different thing from before.

sentence: みんなに祝福されて、うれしかった。
translation: Everyone congratulated us, and I was happy.
note: 祝福されて = being congratulated.
wm: congratulations, blessing
祝福する = to congratulate, to celebrate someone. Hikaru's marriage was 祝福された at first.
sm: People congratulated them and they were happy.
Talking about a wedding or announcement.
sb: みんなに：by everyone
祝福されて、：was congratulated
うれしかった。：was happy
Whole: everyone congratulated us and I was happy.
se: Everyone congratulated us, and I was happy.
I was glad everyone celebrated with us.
It made me happy that everyone congratulated us.

sentence: うちの旦那、料理がうまいんです。
translation: My husband is good at cooking.
wm: husband
Casual way to say husband. 旦那さん = someone else's husband. Hikaru: 元旦那 = ex-husband.
sm: A woman is proud of her husband's cooking.
sb: うちの旦那、：my husband
料理が：cooking
うまいんです。：is good at
Whole: my husband is good at cooking.
se: My husband is good at cooking.
My husband cooks really well.
My hubby's a great cook.

sentence: だんだん寒くなってきたな。
translation: It's gradually getting colder.
wm: gradually, step by step
For slow change over time. Hikaru's ex-wife: だんだん苦しくなって.
sm: The weather is slowly getting colder.
sb: だんだん：gradually
寒くなってきたな。：it's getting colder
Whole: it's gradually getting colder.
se: It's gradually getting colder.
It's slowly getting colder.

sentence: 最終的には、俺が決めた。
